title: The Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
seo_title: Grade 11 Nature of Roots Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Nature of roots: determine the nature of the roots of a quadratic equation using the discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 worksheets: the discriminant, nature of roots, and values of k for equal, real and non-real roots. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Δ = b² − 4ac.
  • Δ < 0: non-real roots. Δ = 0: real, equal roots.
  • Δ > 0: real, unequal roots, rational if Δ is a perfect square and irrational if it is not.
  • Real roots means Δ ≥ 0.

Examples

Example

2x² − 3x − 5 = 0

Δ = 9 + 40 = 49

Answer: real, unequal, rational

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The signΔ = b² − 4ac, so watch negative c.
Rational or irrationalCheck if Δ is a perfect square.
Equal rootsEqual roots: Δ = 0.

faq.a: Determine the nature of the roots of a quadratic equation using the discriminant.
The roots are not real numbers.

faq.q: Can I use Δ for a graph?
faq.a: Yes: it tells you how many x-intercepts there are.
